provenance.scope: A film the museum made of what a work describes, shown as that work's close look. Its lines run under the film, outside the picture: each from its own second of the film until the next line's. The work's own line in lines.json stays the work's.
provenance.rule: A line holds at most 120 characters and 20 words in either language, and no sentence over 14 words. Every line names its source, and the record prints it.
provenance.files: The film's bytes live in the asset store. A record there names this file's key as its `source`, its role (`showpiece-film` or `showpiece-poster`) and its framing; a work whose records the store does not carry opens as it did before.

lines.en: Built on a computer from his notes. Around 1512 he drew the water curling behind the flaps.
lines.de: Nach seinen Notizen am Computer gebaut. Um 1512 zeichnete er, wie das Wasser hinter der Klappe wirbelt.

lines.en: Those curls help shut the valve, as he wrote. Seen in a model in 1968, in living people in 2014.
lines.de: Diese Wirbel helfen der Klappe beim Schließen, wie er schrieb. 1968 sah man sie im Modell, 2014 bei lebenden Menschen.
lines.source: Bellhouse and Bellhouse, Nature 217 (1968). Bissell, Dall'Armellina and Choudhury, European Heart Journal 35 (2014).
